issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Enable verified eager LN fusion for SANA-Video
issues.body:
## Motivation

SANA-Video eager inference inherits the image model's restriction that enables LN+modulation fusion only on CUDA-graph streams. For the tested video activation, `[1, 32760, 2240]`, the existing fused kernel passes live exactness verification. It preserves the required contiguous input copy while fusing LayerNorm, scale and shift, avoiding the intermediate tensors between those operations. A separate final-head profile replaces 82 ATen LayerNorm chains with 82 existing fused kernels per CFG iteration, reducing the total GPU kernel count from 2,309 to 2,063.

The image restriction remains the default: prior image measurements in #34015 found an eager regression. Video opts in at its two transformer-block normalization sites and its final modulated normalization. Main's existing video BCG path already uses this fusion; this PR extends eager execution rather than claiming new BCG support.

Frozen SGLang main: `af21e2b989e482cfdce39689126562f2209d53ac`.
Final tested head: `e0d694593a65cb5b463c4011b84ee50abefa5e43`.
Frozen vLLM-Omni: `817d4c17feb702289a2d2b2cbacfd594c262b7a7`.

## Modifications

- Add an optional `allow_eager=False` keyword to the existing `sana_ln_modulate` wrapper and reuse its existing stream/device/compile dispatch helper.
- Opt in only from SANA-Video's three call sites. Preserve the fused kernel, per-signature live-ATen exactness gate, unverified-capture protection and mismatch fallback.
- Extend the existing four-shape wrapper test across both stream policies, with fresh gate state, default image inference and grad-enabled fallback checks. Reuse the generic gate tests and update the existing kernel README.

No new kernel, environment variable, tuning setting or unrelated refactor is included.

## Accuracy Tests

One physical RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPU0, SM120, 97,887 MiB, 600 W, driver 595.84. GPU1 remains idle. SGLang uses PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 / Triton 3.8.0; Omni uses PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. Dependencies and resolved launch commands are archived.

The common checkpoint is `Efficient-Large-Model/SANA-Video_2B_480p_diffusers@db5f398b13ca086d09a50ce156c20527773841b1`, with verified file hashes. Both native pipelines run 832×480, 81 frames at 16 fps, 50 steps, CFG 6, CPU seed 1101, empty negative prompt, maximum 300 selected text tokens, batch/concurrency 1. DiT and text encoder are BF16; VAE, initial noise and solver arithmetic retain the native FP32 contract. The effective positive text includes the same motion-score instruction. Both encode H.264/yuv420p with CRF 0; native encoder versions differ and all quality comparisons use the same decoder.

Actual runtime observations establish equal token IDs/masks, initial noise, timesteps and sigmas. Native BF16 text-encoder outputs and subsequent model predictions differ across frameworks; they were measured, not replaced. The observer preserves all eight qualification MP4s byte-for-byte.

Cross-framework admission requires **every frame** to satisfy SSIM ≥0.92 and PSNR ≥24 dB:

| Prompt | Mean / minimum SSIM | Mean / minimum PSNR (dB) | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| short | 0.956517 / 0.930914 | 30.7329 / 28.4207 | pass |
| long | 0.962520 / 0.951014 | 30.9685 / 29.1087 | pass |
| Chinese | 0.939182 / 0.920909 | 26.7774 / 23.5768 | **fail at frames 26–28; excluded from performance admission** |

Final main/PR compatibility checks cover eager and BCG, short → long → Chinese → repeated short, lossless → exact → high → lossless, and three separate profile requests. All **51 MP4s and all 81 decoded frames per video** match the corresponding main quality setting exactly. This does not claim that different quality settings match one another or that the baseline's semantic generation defects are fixed.

![SANA-Video 2B 480p, short prompt, actual main/PR frames at 0, 2.5 and 5 seconds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/media/short-main-vs-pr.png)

![SANA-Video 2B 480p, long prompt, actual main/PR frames at 0, 2.5 and 5 seconds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/media/long-main-vs-pr.png)

![SANA-Video 2B 480p, chinese prompt, actual main/PR frames at 0, 2.5 and 5 seconds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/media/chinese-main-vs-pr.png)

Original generated videos: [short main](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/media/videos/short-main.mp4), [short PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/media/videos/short-pr.mp4), [long main](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/media/videos/long-main.mp4), [long PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/media/videos/long-pr.mp4), [chinese main](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/media/videos/chinese-main.mp4), [chinese PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/media/videos/chinese-pr.mp4).

All three representative-frame panels were reviewed: short has two red teapots, long has a duplicated spout-like shape, and Chinese has a malformed stacked lid/handle and cup. These artifacts are identical on main and PR. Representative frames were reviewed; full motion was not watched.

The final existing numerical/gate selection passed **13 tests**. CPU tensors also preserve eager output and actual `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` FX tracing with one graph, without entering or poisoning the fusion gate. This is a CPU fallback check in the CUDA-enabled environment, not a GPU compile benchmark. The initial diagnostic hid CUDA and failed during an existing module's import-time device query; that failure is retained. Re-running the unchanged CPU diagnostic with CUDA visible for import passed, without repeating the already-passing GPU tests.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

| Configuration | Prompt | n | Mean / p50 / p95 E2E (s) | Serial req/s | Request peak GiB | Separate synchronized denoise / decode (s) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| omni_eager | short | 6 | 85.1189 / 85.1176 / 85.1365 | 0.01175 | 31.011 | 81.1538 / 3.2919 (n=1) |
| omni_eager | long | 6 | 85.1154 / 85.1145 / 85.1263 | 0.01175 | 31.011 | 81.1240 / 3.2956 (n=1) |
| main_eager | short | 6 | 63.5963 / 63.5936 / 63.6156 | 0.01572 | 23.054 | 58.5181 / 5.0380 (n=4) |
| main_eager | long | 6 | 63.6024 / 63.6025 / 63.6270 | 0.01572 | 23.054 | 58.5239 / 5.0381 (n=2) |
| v1_eager | short | 12 | 61.8100 / 61.8112 / 61.8227 | 0.01618 | 23.054 | not collected here |
| v1_eager | long | 12 | 61.8118 / 61.8131 / 61.8330 | 0.01618 | 23.054 | not collected here |
| final_eager | short | 12 | 61.8130 / 61.8119 / 61.8314 | 0.01618 | 23.054 | 56.7082 / 5.0372 (n=4) |
| final_eager | long | 12 | 61.8121 / 61.8121 / 61.8288 | 0.01618 | 23.054 | 56.7166 / 5.0373 (n=2) |

Primary values use every predeclared measured request. NVML is sampled every 250 ms during requests; these are observed device-memory peaks, not exact allocator maxima. Denoise is from a separate synchronized diagnostic, not a component subtracted from primary E2E. V1 is retained for cleanup comparison. Omni uses its native synchronized method wrappers, with one steady diagnostic request per English prompt. Native stage boundaries differ across frameworks; no diagnostic timing replaces primary E2E.

| Prompt | Final mean E2E reduction vs main | Omni / final mean E2E | V1 → final mean latency change | Cleanup paired-t 95% regression upper bound |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| short | 2.80412% | 1.377038× | +0.00492% | 0.02248% |
| long | 2.81471% | 1.377001× | +0.00059% | 0.04267% |

| Comparison | Prompt | Process pairs | Paired median geometric ratio | Paired-log-t 95% interval |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| main_vs_final | short | 2 | 1.028797 | [1.028197, 1.029398] |
| omni_vs_final | short | 2 | 1.376901 | [1.374693, 1.379112] |
| omni_vs_main | short | 2 | 1.338359 | [1.336993, 1.339727] |
| v1_vs_final_cleanup | short | 4 | 0.999899 | [0.999775, 1.000023] |
| main_vs_final | long | 2 | 1.028919 | [1.026809, 1.031033] |
| omni_vs_final | long | 2 | 1.376851 | [1.372864, 1.380849] |
| omni_vs_main | long | 2 | 1.338153 | [1.331543, 1.344796] |
| v1_vs_final_cleanup | long | 4 | 0.999953 | [0.999573, 1.000333] |

Intervals use process-pair log ratios, not requests as independent process replicates; only two main/final and Omni/final process pairs limit precision. Cleanup has four predeclared pairs. All original requests and warmups remain in raw evidence.

| Configuration | Cached launch-to-ready min / max (s) |
|---|---:|
| main_eager | 104.121 / 104.133 |
| v1_eager | 102.120 / 102.126 |
| final_eager | 102.119 / 102.126 |
| omni_eager | 28.014 / 28.015 |

These are cached process launches, not cold-start distributions. BCG capture/replay costs and quality transitions are reported separately; this eager opt-in is not new BCG support.

The frozen sequence is M–V1–F–O–V1–F–F–V1–O–F–V1–M, with one excluded warmup and three measured requests per English prompt per process; prompt order reverses in the second half. Main/Omni each have n=6 per prompt, and V1/final each have n=12. All measured final samples are included. Primary HTTP E2E includes submission, native polling where applicable, encoding and complete MP4 transfer, and excludes validation and disk writes. SGLang primary uses no profiler, observer or added stage synchronization. Omni retains its native defaults and fast paths.

The tables report final mean/p50/p95 E2E, serial req/s, observed peak GPU memory, synchronized stage diagnostics and all predeclared paired comparisons. Main A/A's maximum noise statistic was 0.028087%. Cleanup uses four predeclared process pairs: final mean regression must not exceed that A/A noise and the paired log-t 95% upper regression bound must be below 0.1%. Any uncertainty requires an explicit supplemental experiment retaining every original sample, not a favorable-result retry or relaxed threshold.

Final-head synchronized profile, complete CFG iteration 3, joined from CPU launch correlations to GPU kernels:

| Configuration | GPU kernels | Kernel sum (ms) | Fused LN | Graph launches |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| main eager | 2309 | 1170.332 | 0 | 0 |
| PR eager | 2063 | 1134.931 | 82 | 0 |
| main BCG | 2103 | 1135.823 | 82 | 2 |
| PR BCG | 2103 | 1135.529 | 82 | 2 |

The existing 40 RoPE, 40 bias-SiLU and 40 bias-GLU calls are present in every profile. All 82 LN fusions in the BCG profiles are graph-correlated. These diagnostic sums are not primary serving latency.

The named-kernel count difference between final eager and BCG is exactly 40 `memcpy32_post` kernels, totaling 0.0423 ms, about 0.0037% of the step's kernel sum. This count difference is not evidence of a material BCG bottleneck; its originating library operation has not been established by the histogram alone.

Each BCG arm builds one graph with one segment during warmup, then serves 13 requests with **900 model replays and zero serving capture calls**. Exact/high use uncaptured quality-specific eager paths; returning to lossless reuses the same graph. Actual construction took 2.799 s on main and 2.828 s on PR. Complete warmup denoising took 49.176 / 49.203 s; cached launch-to-ready took 104.123 / 106.130 s. These are single cached observations, not cold-start distributions.

Synchronized eager lossless denoise means are main 58.518 / 58.524 s versus final 56.708 / 56.717 s for short/long (n=4/2). BCG lossless means are main 56.742 / 56.746 s versus final 56.728 / 56.731 s. Full-process diagnostic NVML peaks include loading, all quality transitions and profiling where collected; they are not matched serving-only memory estimates. The first main exact-short VAE decode took 10.278 s versus about 3.51 s on subsequent exact requests; this transition cost is retained and is not used as a candidate performance gain.

A separate Omni diagnostic uses the existing native synchronized method profiler. Its representative short/long denoise is 81.154 / 81.124 s and decode is 3.292 / 3.296 s (n=1 each after excluding the first HTTP request). All four diagnostic MP4s and their 81 frame hashes match the original native outputs. Startup also executes a small pipeline warmup; it is retained separately using the actual application-startup log marker. The initial collector counted five forwards instead of four HTTP requests, so its failed assertion is preserved and a corrected offline audit matches each serving timing group to its HTTP response. No GPU request was rerun and no primary sample was replaced.

Final eager and final BCG diagnostic processes each include one profile request and peak at 23,859 / 26,343 MiB, a difference of 2,484 MiB (2.426 GiB). This process-level observation includes warmup, quality switching and profiling; it does not isolate BCG's serving-only memory overhead. Main eager has no profile request, so its process peak is not used for that comparison.

## Cleanup and reproduction

The final diff was fully reviewed against BBuf's cleanup examples #42391, #40265 and #39293. It reuses the existing dispatch helper rather than duplicating stream/grad/device checks, retains only the model opt-in, and extends existing tests rather than introducing a parallel harness into production. All applicable scoped pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed. A final upstream refresh at `1ab008f5b090e6595479ba57934e9211ab083565` found unchanged SANA runtime/kernel/README files; the shared test file only gained an unrelated Joy test block. The tested frozen baseline and head remain unchanged.

Final cleanup mean latency changes are +0.00492% / +0.00059%, below the A/A noise; paired 95% regression upper bounds are 0.02248% / 0.04267%, below the predeclared 0.1% margin. All four cleanup pairs and all requests are retained, including the small positive regression estimates. All 96 primary MP4s match their qualified native arm hashes. The separate [immutable evidence branch](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/tree/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a) contains the [reproduction README](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/README.md), [full results](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/performance-table.md), [frozen 12-process plan](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/evidence/plans/sana-video-ln-final-primary-cleanup1.json), [raw launch/client records](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/tree/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/evidence/block-runs), [A/A admission](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/evidence/preflight/sana-video-main-eager-aa1-admission.json), [final primary and cleanup admission](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/evidence/preflight/sana-video-ln-final-primary-cleanup1-admission.json), [compatibility admission](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/evidence/preflight/sana-video-ln-final-compatibility1-admission.json), [runtime input audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/evidence/preflight/sana-video-runtime-input-audit1.json), [profile attribution](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/evidence/preflight/sana-video-ln-final-profile1.json), [Omni stage audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/evidence/preflight/sana-video-omni-stages1-admission.json), and [actual video identities](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/actual-main-pr-videos.json). All exported files have hashes in [the manifest](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0fb5de3d2989aca1a8a8b8cabdc7e0af228cac5a/evidence-files-sha256.json); the complete archives were independently verified locally.

The exact launchers and client commands are public. With the pinned checkouts, dependencies, checkpoint and directory layout from the README:

```bash
# Host-side fixed sequence; each block starts its own native server.
python3 /data/xyzhang/diffusion-rtx6000-20261026/run_sana_video_blocks1.py \
  /data/xyzhang/diffusion-rtx6000-20261026/sana-video-ln-final-primary-cleanup1.json
```

Use a fresh reproduction directory and restore the required qualified reference metadata from the evidence; the scripts refuse changed source/payload hashes and existing output directories. The recorded Omni base is a local image, whose public pullability is not claimed; full package/source provenance and image identities are disclosed in the README. Code, media, traces and weights remain separate; no large artifacts enter the code PR.

Scope is the tested native single-GPU 480p workload. The 720p checkpoint has a separately retained frozen native latent-shape configuration gap. Other shapes, batch/concurrency extensions, two-GPU operation, GPU compilation and quantization performance remain unrun. This PR does not establish a new beneficial BCG scenario or full-matrix dominance.

issues.title: [Fix] diffusion: Check cancellation at stage and sampling boundaries
issues.body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #47055. Cancellation was coupled to progress-bar updates, which are not always sampling-step boundaries: some samplers update infrequently or once per chunk. A cancellation during encoding, decoding, or after the last sampling step could also miss the opportunity to skip later work.

## Changes

- Check at executor stage boundaries on every replica rank, outside rank-selective branches. Retain the original requests even when the final stage returns `OutputBatch`.
- Move sampling checks out of `ReportingTqdm` into `PipelineStage.check_cancelled`. Preserve the existing custom-sampler integrations and check inside SANA-WM streaming chunks. Grouped sampling checks the complete request group, not only its first request.
- Check after forward, before saving or handing finalization to a background thread. Sequential execution consumes the current output before checking, so cancellation cannot shift the remaining outputs between requests.
- Keep disabled checks lightweight. Reuse existing residency cleanup, cancellation transport, and all-members-cancelled semantics. No new options or production modules.
- Document checkpoint placement for custom pipelines and the API's cancellation limits.

Existing production files: +78/-39 lines. Tests and docs: +218/-56 lines.

## Validation

- Seven targeted test files on an isolated GPU development machine: **195 passed, 2 subtests passed**.
- Includes real two-process Gloo stage-boundary tests for replicated and rank-only stages, terminal `OutputBatch`, cleanup, low-frequency progress updates, sequential output ordering, deferred finalization, and SANA-WM inner-step cancellation. Also runs existing video lifecycle, executor, MOVA, SANA-Video2 and Kandinsky6-SR tests.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks pass.

**Native GPU validation:** Wan2.1 T2V 1.3B, 2 x H200, Ulysses 2, BF16/resident weights, FA, eager, 832x480, 17 frames, 8 steps, seed 42. Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, diffusers 0.37.0, pyzmq 27.2.0. The same warm process alternated non-cancellable/cancellable requests in A-B-B-A order, eight samples per arm, with conditioning caching, progress reporting and saving enabled in both arms and stage-profiling synchronization disabled.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Saved-output E2E median, checks off / on | 0.8208 s / 0.8261 s (+0.64%) |
| Cancel a 50-step request after progress step 20 | Stops before decoding; no output saved |
| Pre-cancelled request | Does not enter the pipeline |
| Normal request after both cancellations | Completes successfully |
| 17 comparable completed MP4s | Byte-identical SHA-256 |

This measures the check toggle on this head, not branch-vs-main performance or all-model throughput. GPU validation uses a diagnostic SDK harness through the real scheduler, ZMQ and distributed workers, not an additional live HTTP E2E test. DELETE integration is covered by the lifecycle/IPC tests. The diagnostic SDK logs cancelled outputs as errors, and shutdown emits the existing CUDA IPC producer-lifetime warning; neither is claimed fixed here. The development environment uses `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1`; CI remains the supported-environment regression gate.

## Limits

This is cooperative cancellation, not kernel preemption. Rank-only stages finish before their executor checkpoint; already-running saves/uploads are not interrupted. Disaggregated and multi-node cancellation remain outside the scope inherited from #47055. A new custom sampler must use the documented checkpoint API; arbitrary inner loops are not intercepted automatically.

issues.body:
## Motivation

Roles should describe where pipeline stages run, rather than require a new hardcoded role and payload for each split. This adds an experimental, opt-in stage deployment path on top of the existing generation API and Mooncake transport.

Targets `main`; the prerequisite #45309 has landed. Main has been merged, not rebased.

## Modifications

- Declare stage groups, worker endpoints, replicas, node placement, and per-role server arguments in a deployment file. Select stages by registered name or zero-based index.
- Transfer the complete request context automatically between consecutive stage groups, including nested tensors, scheduler state, and consumed RNG state. Tensor data uses the tensor transport; tracing, metrics, and model modules remain process-local.
- Retain explicit-field contracts for parallel encoder branches and fan-out/join graphs. Automatic context transfer does not infer parallel branches.
- Load only the selected role's components and construct its stages through factories. Separate standard decoder postprocessing into a stage while retaining monolithic result handling.
- Add local node launch, bounded admission/result leases, cancellation cleanup, scalar-tensor transport support, and explicit remote error propagation.
- Support directly targeted encoder pools with `EncodingClient.encode(..., role=...)`, independent checkpoint/configuration per role, and independently sized replica pools. Same-model roles preserve explicit settings while recalculating automatic defaults for their GPU count.
- Add scoped, bounded, input-ordered client prefetch. Receive copies use a dedicated CUDA stream and do not block the event loop while completing; cancellation waits for the copy before recycling the receive slot.
- Update the generic disaggregation guide, CLI reference, and model integration guidance. Add focused unit coverage and a reusable manual cross-model E2E matrix.

## Accuracy Tests

### Encoder-pool follow-up (2026-10-27)

- Linux H200, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130: **377 tests and 191 subtests passed**, including the public-checkpoint manual E2E test and the deployment/server-args/disaggregation unit suites. Required pre-commit hooks passed.
- Public-model E2E: two Z-Image Turbo text encoder replicas plus one FLUX.2 Klein 4B VAE replica. Tests exercise role-specific model loading through the node launcher, direct pool calls, combined outputs, different prompt lengths and image sizes, ordered prefetch, early exit, invalid-role recovery, and zero remaining coordinator leases/jobs. Conditioning caching is disabled in this test; repeated tensors compare with `rtol=atol=0`.
- Separately validated Mooncake RDMA tensor returns between two GPU pods on **one physical H200 host**. BF16 prompt embeddings and image latents arrived on the client GPU and matched separate/combined role calls exactly. This follow-up does not claim a new cross-physical-node test or a training-throughput improvement.
- Public docs include a mixed-checkpoint 2:1 pool deployment and scoped client examples. Encoder outputs retain each model stage's existing semantics; arbitrary hidden-layer extraction, training-specific VAE representations, cross-process autograd, and dynamic batching are not implied.

### Earlier generation validation

Validation used Linux H200 workers and independent monolithic references with matched precision, attention backend, stage parallelism, and VAE layout. Output comparisons used `rtol=atol=0`.

| Coverage | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Independent encoder / denoiser / decoder: Wan2.1-1.3B, Z-Image Turbo, Qwen Image | Passed |
| FLUX.2 Klein 4B: reference-image VAE encoding and T2I | Passed |
| Sana 600M and Anima: different stage orders, custom conditioning, multi-output requests | Passed |
| Z-Image TP2, Z-Image Ulysses2 with an odd patch grid, Wan TP2 x Ulysses2 | 3 passed in 448.82s |
| Two physical H200 nodes, Mooncake RDMA: Z-Image and Wan TP2 x Ulysses2 | All compared outputs had max absolute difference 0 |

The matrix varies resolution, steps, and seed; checks repeated and concurrent requests; and verifies recovery after invalid requests. FLUX.1-schnell was attempted but blocked by checkpoint access, so it is not counted as validated.

- At `fd59d2b6125`: 25 deployment unit tests passed, including the direct file entrypoint. The multi-rank matrix above also passed at this revision.
- Earlier at `8ed79b61785`: 448 tests plus 139 subtests passed, and the existing explicit FLUX.3 encoder graph passed both E2E cases. This broader suite was not rerun at the final revision.
- Cross-node runs used `40eca988b5f`; subsequent changes through `fd59d2b6125` only changed tests/docs.

issues.title: [Fix] diffusion: Exit the worker after an unrecoverable device error
issues.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #38167.

When a diffusion forward fails with a CUDA error other than OOM (a driver error, a device-side assert, a caching-allocator assert), the device or its allocator can no longer be trusted. The worker logged the error, called `empty_cache()` and kept serving. Every later request either ran on the broken device or failed, and `/health` still returned `{"status": "ok"}`, so no orchestrator would restart the server.

In #38167 the trigger is PyTorch's expandable-segments allocator (pytorch/pytorch#188008, on WSL2 with `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`). That needs a PyTorch fix. This PR makes the server fail cleanly instead of staying up broken.

## Modifications

This builds on the fail-closed path from #46025 instead of adding a separate unhealthy flag.

- `gpu_worker.py`: classify forward errors that leave the device unusable (`torch.AcceleratorError`, `CUDA driver error:`, `CUDA error:`, `HIP error:`, caching-allocator asserts, also through `__cause__`/`__context__`; anything mentioning "out of memory" is excluded). On one, log the restart guidance and raise `_FatalDeviceError`, a `SystemExit` like `_FatalDistributedForward`, so it escapes request-level recovery and skips `empty_cache()`. `run_scheduler_process` catches both and calls `os._exit(1)`.
- The HTTP server's backend monitor from #46025 then fails pending requests, rejects new POSTs with 503 and turns `/health` 503. OOM keeps its current recover-and-continue behavior on a single GPU.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. Successful requests take the same path as before.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. Nothing changes on a successful request.

## Tests

Live server on an RTX A6000 (torch 2.14.1+cu130, `Efficient-Large-Model/Sana_600M_512px_diffusers`). A temporary hook, not part of this PR, writes out of bounds on the GPU before `forward_fn()` when the prompt contains a marker, raising a real `CUDA error: device-side assert triggered`.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Normal request | 200 (3.2 s) |
| `/health` before | 200 |
| Request that triggers the assert | 500 after 1.1 s |
| Request queued 0.3 s behind it | 500 after 0.8 s |
| `/health` after, polled from 1.3 s to 11.6 s | 503 `{"status":"unhealthy","error":"Scheduler worker exited; restart the server."}` |
| New request | 503 in 1 ms |
| Scheduler process | exited (`<defunct>` until reaped) |
| GPU memory | 13.5 GB used before, 0.27 GB after |

No `empty_cache()` call after the error. Not covered: multi-rank runs and the original expandable-segments failure from #38167, which can't be triggered on demand.

Unit: `multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_unrecoverable_device_error.py` (CPU) covers the classifier and the exit path.

issues.title: [Diffusion] Preserve mapped component weights during low-memory offload
issues.body:
## Motivation

Component offload (`--component-residency <c>=component-offload`, and the legacy
`--*-cpu-offload` flags) swapped a component out with
`module.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)` — a full device-to-host copy of **immutable**
weights into fresh host memory on every single swap-out. Three problems this PR removes:

1. **A wasted D2H copy per swap-out.** Inference never mutates weights. Measured on
   MiniMax-H3's 9.7 GiB video VAE on an RTX 5090: 4.85 s on the first cycle, 0.37 s per
   cycle after; now ~0 (one device sync + a pointer rebind).
2. **Unbudgeted, kernel-locked host memory.** `module.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)`
   allocates a *pinned* destination, entirely behind `HostPinBudget`'s back — 9.7 GiB per
   offloaded VAE that the kernel can never reclaim, RssAnon never shows, and no
   accounting ever sees. Pinned offload memory now goes through the budget, and a denial
   degrades to the existing pageable storage without copying anything.
3. **`keep_checkpoint_mapped` weights were destroyed after one use.** A VAE loaded as
   mmap views into its safetensors file (so a constrained host keeps those bytes
   evictable) lost the mapping permanently on the first GPU round trip. The mapping now
   survives: a mapped weight's host copy *is* its mmap view, never replaced.

## Modifications

Five commits:

1. **BCG × offloaded-DiT guard** (`runtime/server_args/server_args.py`). Any explicitly
   non-resident DiT placement with `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph` fails at startup
   validation, next to the other BCG rules: BCG captures the DiT forward, every offload
   flavor rebinds or frees its weight storage between forwards, and a captured graph
   replays capture-time addresses. An auto-selected placement disables BCG with a
   warning; non-DiT components stay free to offload.
2. **Pin-budget divisor** (`runtime/managers/memory_managers/host_memory_budget.py`).
   `HostPinBudget` divides by the node-local worker count (`num_gpus // nnodes`) so N
   ranks stop booking the same host headroom N times; the reserve is taken from the
   per-rank share. A denial degrades to pageable hosting, while the overcommit it
   prevents ends in unreclaimable pinned memory and the OOM killer. Single-GPU
   deployments are unaffected.
3. **Dead-line removal** in `layerwise_offload._ensure_mapped_courier`.
4. **Regression test**: a component-offload GPU round trip must preserve the checkpoint
   mapping (fails on the old strategy, flipped by the next commit).
5. **The host-store rewrite**
   (`runtime/managers/memory_managers/component_residency_strategies.py`). Adopts
   layerwise offload's own storage model at component granularity: a
   `ComponentHostStore` captures the checkpoint-time host weights once (mmap views stay
   mmap views; the rest is pinned within a `HostPinBudget` grant, falling back to
   pageable when the budget declines) and hangs off the module. Swap-in copies
   host-to-device on the prefetch stream and rebinds via `.data`; swap-out rebinds every
   parameter to a shared one-element device placeholder — exactly a released layerwise
   layer, so no D2H copy and no new host allocation, ever. The store survives
   strategy-cache rebuilds, releases its device copy on sleep, and stays coherent with
   writers through the layerwise contracts: weight refits route through
   `update_host_weights` (the `update_cpu_weights` analog) and LoRA merge/unmerge wraps
   mutation in `begin`/`end_host_update`, which re-resolves targets after layer
   replacement. The residency report walks the store like `layerwise_offload_managers`.
   DTensor components work through the same `to_local_tensor`/`wrap_for_target` helpers
   layerwise uses. MPS and FSDP routing are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerics change — the same weight bytes reach the device; only where they rest and how
they travel changes. End-to-end MiniMax-H3 (fl2va t2va, 672x384/4 s/8 steps, cookbook
5090 flags with `video_vae=component-offload`, 3 consecutive requests per side) produced
identical outputs on old and new sides.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Component offload is a cookbook-recommended placement for encoder/VAE-sized components.
The real 9.7 GiB H3 video-VAE checkpoint (mmap-loaded, `assign=True`) driven through
`ComponentOffloadStrategy` prepare/finish cycles on a 1× RTX 5090 (32 GB):

| per swap cycle | old strategy | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| swap-out wall | 4.85 s first, 0.37 s after (full D2H) | **~0 s** (sync + rebind) |
| swap-in wall (steady) | 0.37 s (from its pinned copy) | 0.56 s (straight from the mapping) |
| host state at rest | 9.7 GiB **pinned**, unbudgeted; mapping destroyed | 9.7 GiB **still checkpoint-mapped**; zero committed host bytes |
| device bytes per swap-in | 9.71 GiB | 9.71 GiB |

The mapped host copy trades ~0.2 s of swap-in against holding zero committed host
memory; weights the budget grants pinning keep the pinned fast path on both directions.
End-to-end H3 latency is neutral to within noise — the change is memory correctness, not
a latency claim.

Notes:
- `text_encoder=component-offload` cannot work on a 32 GB card for H3 (66.7 GB bf16
  encoder; whole-module swap-in OOMs — verified empirically). The cookbook's layerwise
  placement for it is the right one.
- 5 tests under `test/unit/realtime/`, `test/unit/sana_wm/`, and
  `test_consistency_metrics.py` fail on origin/main, unrelated to this PR; the companion
  `diffusion-fix-unit-tests` branch fixes them separately.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (One case per failure mode: the keep-mapped round trip; residency buckets stable across swap cycles with values intact; budget denial degrades without copying; both writer paths reach the host store; the BCG guard's raise/disable/ignore cases; the N-rank budget divisor and per-rank-share reserve. Full `multimodal_gen/test/unit` on the 5090 is green except the 5 pre-existing main failures fixed in the companion branch — both together: 2191 passed, 0 failed.)
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No flag semantics change; existing docs remain accurate.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (See the sections above.)

issues.title: [Feat] diffusion: Plan reversible residency before warmup
issues.body:
## Summary

- inventory the selected checkpoint components before loading and seed a conservative resident set that the post-load planner can fully replace
- plan complete resident, component-offload, and partial layerwise target states across DiTs, encoders, VAEs, lazy components, and two-stage pipelines, including independent resident counts and implicit policies per repeated layer group
- use temporary manager-level warmup counters and denoising-stage attribution so repeated layer groups, including non-standard component keys, receive independent residency choices while one-shot or unused groups do not consume stage-resident VRAM
- use one exact selection vector for every rank/phase VRAM constraint, placement-transition scratch, replica-pooled HostPin allowance, and host repacking headroom; assign per-rank pin quotas only after the joint solve
- account the full persistent host-store footprint when an ordinary resident component first becomes layerwise; reuse existing CPU weights and charge only incremental repacking scratch from component offload
- charge complete apply-time device deltas for coarse/layerwise transitions, and model prefetch with the same weight footprint as active use for all current strategies
- run the same startup sequence for server and offline entrypoints: static placement, one representative warmup, and at most one measured adjustment; resident-only verification is one full-shape step
- preserve the current HostPin layout during static weight-only planning and construct the complete pin frontier only after the representative warmup can score it
- keep loader-required placement fixed for LTX2.3 `original` mode, retain allocator reserve after the realized placement runs, and let numerically non-invariant pipelines decline automatic residency changes

## Design boundary

The preload decision is a replaceable load-feasibility seed, not an independent serving optimizer. Its load VRAM budget is a separate lifecycle feasibility constraint; it is never composed after the fact as an independently optimal serving decision. The serving solve uses one selection vector for every runtime phase VRAM, placement transition, and node HostPin constraint. Once modules have exact sizes, static planning may demote or replace every seeded component before the first forward; warmup then validates and refines the complete serving frontier with measured workload phases and latency utility.

Structural loading choices such as explicit FSDP remain outside this planner because changing them after calibration requires reloading weights. Explicit/online quantization and direct GPU loading likewise fix only their affected components; unrelated components in the same pipeline remain eligible for measured placement. The exactness guarantee is therefore relative to the supplied replaceable placement frontier, resource estimates, and target workload, rather than a claim about startup-plus-serving lifecycle cost.

Within one request replica, multi-process HostPin is pooled into the same placement solve, so TP/SP/PP/CFG ranks may receive asymmetric quotas while their sum remains bounded. Different DP replicas retain disjoint local-worker shares rather than coordinating one cross-replica solve; homogeneous startup remains symmetric, while heterogeneous DP workloads are outside the exactness claim. Quotas are applied transactionally and rollback restores the prior allocation.

## Validation

### B200: Wan2.2 A14B NVFP4, 640x384x17, 12 steps

The load-safe seed selected both DiTs resident. The text encoder and VAE retained their native layerwise loading semantics; the 4-step full-shape probe then selected both resident. This preserves checkpoint/model initialization behavior while moving serving placement out of model-specific thresholds. The post-adjustment pass validates the complete serving shape; resident-only changes use one denoise step because they remove hooks/transfers without changing the compute path.

| metric | old-head CI result |
|---|---:|
| startup to ready | 80.4 s |
| E2E | 2740.56 ms |
| average denoise | 209.78 ms |
| load / runtime peak | 25182 / 52378 MiB |
| consistency | passed |

### Conservative preload boundary

A 29.7 GiB Wan2.1 1.3B experiment showed why checkpoint bytes alone cannot promote auxiliary modules safely: a weight-only plan exhausted activation headroom near 29.1 GiB and then paid for layerwise recovery. LTX2.3 showed the same issue on a larger request. The production preload seed therefore covers native DiTs only; encoders and VAEs retain their configured loading path until the bounded full-shape probe supplies activation evidence.

The old-head NVIDIA run passed unit, BCG, component-accuracy, B200, RTX 5090, four of five H100 1-GPU partitions, and one completed H100 2-GPU partition before the three known long-running partitions were cancelled to avoid seven retries against stale VRAM guards. The current-head run validates workload-faithful CI sampling, resident-only one-step validation, and explicit before/after calibration timing.

Focused tests cover initial placement, the exact joint solver, per-rank checkpoint loading, HostPin accounting, layerwise transitions, and warmup/rollback orchestration. Changed-file and merge-conflict pre-commit passed on `93f1464c2af64`. The current head preserves node-pooled HostPin and per-group policy choices, avoids speculative pin-frontier construction before calibration, and collapses a measured pin frontier only when every rank-local share and the exact per-component latency cap prove it non-binding.

Completed H100 evidence from parent run `33183409022` additionally showed why both planner layers are needed: LTX2.3 HQ selected a live-allocation-feasible layout whose mapped allocator pool left no request reserve, while SANA-WM changed numerics after runtime promotion. The stack now combines the child branch allocation-gap correction during candidate planning with the parent post-placement peak-reserved guard, fixes both LTX DiTs in `original` mode, and keeps SANA-WM on its proven static placement. No additional warmup or retry round was added.

issues.title: [Feat] diffusion: Native SANA-Sprint support
issues.body:
## Motivation

Closes #43671. Joint work with @raghulchandramouli, who independently found the SANA 1.5 qk_norm bug on #43671; his commits are listed under *Joint contributions*.

[SANA-Sprint 0.6B](https://huggingface.co/Efficient-Large-Model/Sana_Sprint_0.6B_1024px_diffusers) is a guidance-distilled SANA variant that generates 1024px images in 1–4 steps. Its checkpoint declares `SanaSprintPipeline` and `SCMScheduler`, and neither had a native implementation. This reuses the SANA transformer, Gemma2 encoder and DC-AE, and adds Sprint's pipeline, scheduler and defaults.

## Modifications

- **`SCMScheduler`** (`runtime/models/schedulers/scheduling_scm.py`): subclasses Diffusers' TrigFlow sCM scheduler. Diffusers' `SanaSprintPipeline` does three things inline in its loop: it rescales the DiT input, converts the DiT's flow prediction to TrigFlow, and divides the final sample by `sigma_data`. Here `scale_model_input` / `step` / `init_noise_sigma` do that work, so the shared `DenoisingStage` loop runs Sprint unchanged. `timesteps` holds the sCM timesteps the DiT is conditioned on. The 2-step intermediate angle (1.3) is applied only for 2 steps, so 1/3/4 steps work without passing `intermediate_timesteps=None` as Diffusers requires.
- **SANA DiT** (`runtime/models/dits/sana.py`):
  - `guidance_embeds` checkpoints get `SanaCombinedTimestepGuidanceEmbeddings`, with Diffusers' module layout and weight names.
  - `qk_norm="rms_norm_across_heads"` is now applied in both the linear self-attention and the cross-attention.
  - The arch default for `qk_norm` changes to `None`, matching Diffusers. SANA 1.0 configs omit the key and have no norm weights.
- **Pipeline** (`runtime/pipelines/sana_sprint.py`, `configs/pipeline_configs/sana_sprint.py`, `configs/sample/sana_sprint.py`):
  - Sprint's "complex human instruction" prompt prefix. It reuses SANA-Video's text stage; the instruction is now a class attribute there, and SANA-Video's behavior is unchanged.
  - Per-request embedded guidance: `guidance_scale × guidance_embeds_scale`, rounded to the DiT dtype as Diffusers does.
  - fp32 latents.
  - Defaults: 2 steps, `guidance_scale=4.5`. CFG never runs, so negative prompts are ignored.
  - **Resolution binning**, on by default as in Diffusers (`use_resolution_binning`). The DiT runs at the closest 1024px aspect-ratio bin, then a Sprint decoding stage resizes and center-crops the image back to the requested size. The bin table copies Diffusers' `ASPECT_RATIO_1024_BIN`: importing it pulls in the whole PixArt pipeline (about 8.5 s), so a unit test asserts the copy still matches.
  - **Schedule overrides** per request: `max_timesteps`, `intermediate_timesteps` and explicit `trigflow_timesteps` (`num_inference_steps + 1` decreasing angles). They are validated at admission (a bad schedule returns HTTP 400: angles must lie in [0, 1.5708], explicit schedules must end at 0, and an explicit `intermediate_timesteps` applies only to 2 steps) and declared in `image_request_extra_fields`, so the image API forwards them. Diffusers 0.37's own custom-`timesteps` path raises a `TypeError`, because `retrieve_timesteps` omits `num_inference_steps` for `SCMScheduler`, so explicit angles are checked against Diffusers' scheduler directly.
  - The SANA detector excludes Sprint ids, and `sana_sprint` registers before generic SANA.
- **Tests:**
  - `test/unit/test_sana_sprint.py` (CPU).
  - 1-GPU server cases `sana_sprint_0.6b_t2i` and `sana_sprint_1.6b_t2i` with component accuracy enabled. Perf and consistency checks are off, as for `sana_video_2b_t2v`.
  - A component-accuracy hook branch: Sprint's DiT takes the same guidance value as Diffusers, not the FLUX-style ×1000.
- **Component-accuracy harness fix** (`component_accuracy/utils.py`): `normalize_state_key` rewrites `scale` to `weight`, which turned DC-AE's `to_qkv_multiscale.*` into `to_qkv_multiweight.*`. Prefix-stripped and suffix candidates were built only from that rewritten name, so 36 of 375 VAE parameters never transferred and any DC-AE case failed at 90.4% matched. Candidates are now derived from the original name too; when the two names are equal, the candidate order is unchanged.
- **Docs:** SANA-Sprint entry in the model catalog.

### Side effect: SANA 1.5 now loads its QK-norm weights

SANA 1.5 checkpoints ship trained `attn1/attn2.norm_q/norm_k` weights in every block. sglang's SANA DiT had no such parameters, so the loader skipped those weights with a warning and served the model without QK-norm. With this PR they load. DiT output against Diffusers' `SanaTransformer2DModel` on `SANA1.5_1.6B_1024px_diffusers` (real weights, fixed random inputs, bf16):

| | `norm_q`/`norm_k` params | rel. L2 vs Diffusers | cosine |
|---|---|---|---|
| upstream main | 0 | 25.0% | 0.969 |
| this PR | 80 | 3.5% | 0.9994 |

SANA 1.0 (600M / 1600M) is unaffected: no `qk_norm` in config, so no norm modules are built.

### Joint contributions from raghulchandramouli

- **SANA-Sprint 1.6B** (`Sana_Sprint_1.6B_1024px_diffusers`) is registered by exact id next to 0.6B, in the registry, the registry test and the model catalog. Its configs differ from 0.6B only in transformer size.
- **`test/unit/test_sana_dit_param_names.py`** (CPU) builds the native and Diffusers DiTs on the meta device for six real configs (SANA 1.0 600M/1600M, SANA 1.5 1.6B/4.8B, Sprint 0.6B/1.6B) and runs the loader's own name mapping. It asserts that every checkpoint weight lands on a native parameter of the same shape, and that no native parameter is left unloaded. Against main's DiT, the four configs with qk_norm or guidance embeddings fail; SANA 1.0 passes.
- **Scheduler review and schedule validation fixes.** Out-of-range TrigFlow angles used to reach the DiT (for example, `max_timesteps=2.3562` gave a timestep of about -9e4) and are now rejected at admission. An explicit `intermediate_timesteps` with steps other than 2 used to be dropped silently and is now rejected, as in Diffusers. The review also led to the `pred_original_sample` note in `SCMScheduler.step`'s docstring.

## Test

**Scheduler:** `test_scm_scheduler_reproduces_diffusers_sprint_loop` runs a deterministic stand-in for the bf16 DiT through Diffusers' `SanaSprintPipeline` loop and through the shared-loop call order, for 1, 2 and 4 steps. The outputs match bit for bit (`atol=0`). While writing it I caught a dtype issue: a 0-dim fp32 coefficient times a bf16 DiT output stays bf16, which drifted by about 1e-2. The scheduler now upcasts explicitly, and the test fails if that upcast is removed.

**Component accuracy, 0.6B (1-GPU harness):** all three checks pass. Before the harness fix above, the VAE check failed on weight transfer.

| component | CosSim vs Diffusers/HF |
|---|---|
| transformer (with guidance + qk_norm) | 0.999985 |
| text encoder (Gemma2) | 0.999829 |
| VAE (DC-AE) | 0.999781 |

**End to end vs Diffusers, 0.6B** (`SanaSprintPipeline`, bf16 DiT, VAE upcast to fp32 to match sglang). Same seed (42), 1024×1024, `guidance_scale=4.5`, image PSNR:

| prompt | 1 step | 2 steps | 4 steps |
|---|---|---|---|
| a tiny astronaut hatching from an egg on the moon | 37.0 dB | 33.8 dB | 36.9 dB |
| a red fox sitting in fresh snow, golden hour, photorealistic | 37.3 dB | 42.6 dB | 40.3 dB |
| an isometric illustration of a cozy library with plants and warm lamps | 27.4 dB | 27.7 dB | 28.1 dB |

**Resolution binning and schedule overrides vs Diffusers** (fox prompt, seed 42, 2 steps):

| request | output size (sglang = Diffusers) | PSNR |
|---|---|---|
| 1000×700 (bin 1216×832, resized back) | 700×1000 | 39.2 dB |
| 800×1200 | 1200×800 | 33.8 dB |
| 960×640 | 640×960 | 39.2 dB |
| `intermediate_timesteps=1.1` | 1024×1024 | 41.1 dB |

Over HTTP, explicit `trigflow_timesteps=[1.5708, 1.3, 0]` reproduces the default 2-step image bit for bit. A custom 4-angle schedule produces a clean image. A malformed schedule returns 400 with the reason.

The third prompt is the most detailed image; it keeps the same composition, with fine-detail differences. I traced the gap: there is no single divergence point. Each block differs from Diffusers by about 0.3% (bf16 rounding), and the 28 blocks amplify that to about 7% at the output. Diffusers' own bf16 DiT is just as far from its fp32 run:

| DiT input (real, from the pipeline) | Diffusers bf16 vs fp32 | sglang bf16 vs fp32 | sglang vs Diffusers (bf16) |
|---|---|---|---|
| prompt 1 | 5.0% | 5.5% | 3.8% |
| prompt 3 | 10.1% | 10.2% | 6.9% |

So sglang's output is as close to fp32 as Diffusers' bf16 path is. Switching sglang's linear attention to Diffusers' fp32 formulation, or the caption RMSNorm eps to 1e-5, does not reduce the gap.

**Component accuracy, 1.6B** (1-GPU harness, RTX A6000): all three checks pass.

| component | CosSim vs Diffusers/HF |
|---|---|
| transformer (with guidance + qk_norm) | 0.999979 |
| text encoder (Gemma2) | 0.999829 |
| VAE (DC-AE) | 0.999781 |

**End to end vs Diffusers, 1.6B** (same setup as 0.6B), image PSNR:

| prompt | 1 step | 2 steps | 4 steps |
|---|---|---|---|
| a tiny astronaut hatching from an egg on the moon | 30.0 dB | 26.7 dB | 28.3 dB |
| a red fox sitting in fresh snow, golden hour, photorealistic | 26.2 dB | 26.5 dB | 25.3 dB |
| an isometric illustration of a cozy library with plants and warm lamps | 29.0 dB | 26.7 dB | 28.0 dB |

1.6B scores lower than 0.6B, but the images keep the same composition, pose and lighting and differ only in fine texture. Against an fp32 Diffusers reference (`SanaSprintPipeline` in fp32, TF32 off), both bf16 paths land about equally far away, and sglang is never further:

| prompt | sglang bf16 vs fp32 (1 / 2 / 4 steps) | Diffusers bf16 vs fp32 (1 / 2 / 4 steps) |
|---|---|---|
| astronaut | 28.0 / 25.5 / 26.7 dB | 28.0 / 25.5 / 26.3 dB |
| fox | 26.2 / 27.1 / 28.8 dB | 26.7 / 25.4 / 25.3 dB |
| library | 28.0 / 25.9 / 26.9 dB | 28.1 / 25.8 / 26.8 dB |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

RTX A6000, 1024×1024, warm requests (ms, three runs; the first is cold):

| steps | sglang | Diffusers |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 12174 (cold), 655, 623 | 4704 (cold), 640, 685 |
| 2 | 695, 698, 741 | 755, 756, 725 |
| 4 | 895, 1004, 840 | 1020, 933, 955 |

Comparable latency. Sprint is not admitted to Breakable CUDA Graph or other fast paths in this PR. `perf_baselines/h100.json` gets entries for both new cases because the server test requires them, but their numbers (0.6B: load ~61 s, e2e ~11.8 s cold, `estimated_full_test_time_s=108.4`; 1.6B: load ~62 s, e2e ~0.39 s, `estimated_full_test_time_s=86.1`) were measured on the A6000, not an H100. They only feed CI sharding while `run_perf_check=False`, so please regenerate them on H100 if you want an accurate shard estimate.

## Test environment

- GPU: 1× NVIDIA RTX A6000 (48 GB, sm_86), driver 610.43.02
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5, 6 vCPU
- Software: Python 3.12.13, torch 2.14.1+cu130, diffusers 0.37.0, transformers 5.19.0, nvcc 13.0.88
- Base: measured on upstream `main` at 363e6c6b4d, then rebased onto 79eb10e182 (the 7 commits in between touch no diffusion code; the Sprint, SANA-Video, registry and harness unit tests re-pass after the rebase)

## Tests run

- `test/unit/test_sana_sprint.py`: 10 passed (14 after the joint commits). They cover the scheduler against Diffusers' Sprint loop, including intermediate-angle and explicit-angle schedules; schedule validation; image-API field forwarding; binning (table, bin choice, latent shape, resize/crop); registry; and the `qk_norm` default. Each case was checked to fail with its targeted change reverted: the bf16 upcast, the `qk_norm` default, the registry priority, binning ignoring its flag, the scheduler ignoring explicit angles, and an undeclared API field.
- `test/unit/test_sana_dit_param_names.py`: 6 passed. This and `test_sana_sprint.py` were re-run on Linux CPU at 527ebc9, after merging main, along with the cfg-warmup and OpenAI image-API unit tests (252 passed).
- Unit tests touching the SANA DiT, SANA-Video stages, registry, OpenAI request helpers, component-accuracy harness, GPU cases or perf baselines: 984 passed.
- `test/server/test_server_1_gpu.py -k sana_sprint`: 2 passed (0.6B and 1.6B). Component accuracy: 3 passed for each of 0.6B and 1.6B.

Not done here:
- **TP/SP.** SANA's DiT has none, and its GLUMBConv feed-forward would need halo exchange to shard spatially. For a 0.6B model running at about 0.7 s per image, it isn't worth it.
- **BCG admission.** I'll do it as a follow-up with the eager-vs-BCG byte-identity and A/B timing evidence that admission requires.
- **CLI flags for the new per-request fields.** The shared sampling parser asks that no model-specific fields be added there. The fields work through the HTTP and Python APIs.
- **Binning for plain SANA.** Diffusers' `SanaPipeline` also bins by default and sglang's SANA does not. That would change existing SANA outputs, so it is left out of this PR.

issues.title: [Fix] diffusion: Respect ancestor cgroup memory headroom
issues.body:
## Motivation

Diffusion host-memory planning can overcommit pinned memory when a parent cgroup has a larger limit but less remaining headroom than the child. For example, a child using 10GiB of 32GiB under a parent using 60GiB of 64GiB has 4GiB remaining, not 22GiB. Sibling usage counts against the parent.

## Modifications

Select the ancestor with the least `max(0, limit - usage)` rather than the least numeric limit. Apply the existing file-cache exclusion before comparison. Extend the existing budget tests with four v1/v2 cases, including cache-adjusted headroom.

## Accuracy Tests

2026-10-21 refresh: the complete changed host-budget test file now also runs through normal package imports in official SGLang nightly `0.5.23.dev20261020+g55b2aef7ad` (PyTorch 2.14.1): baseline 4 failed / 32 passed, candidate **36 passed**. A fresh paired real-SANA nested-cgroup repeat retains pixel-identical images and zero OOM/OOM-kill events. [Nightly unit and paired model evidence](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/b967070464b4c7b45eb9c8c044862fedf43a3ec6/validation/rtx5090-20261017/round3/README.md).

| Check | Baseline | Candidate |
|---|---|---|
| Extended host-budget file | 4 failed / 32 passed | 36 passed |
| Actual delegated cgroup v2 + 512MiB anonymous sibling | Overstates headroom and accepts a 128MiB allowance | Rejects that allowance |
| Real SANA 600M, live nested cgroups, one streamed / 27 resident DiT blocks | Books 41,292,288 persistent pinned bytes | Keeps the streamed block pageable |

Both SANA prompts complete with pixel-identical outputs; both arms have zero OOM/OOM-kill events. Ordinary GPU-resident SANA outputs also match. No production OOM was deliberately induced. The isolated fixture releases its unused allocator/cache pages, then calibrates actual cgroup limits once; the production budget calculation is unchanged apart from this patch.

SANA revision: `28f3af7689de15f3883d5863059a2fca0aa9b829` of `Efficient-Large-Model/Sana_600M_1024px_diffusers`, RTX 5090, TP=1, eager, 512×512, two prompts. **Both model arms use the same AutoencoderDC checkpoint-loading prerequisite whose root fix is already in #44690. That prerequisite is not included in this PR.** The budget unit/live-cgroup probes do not depend on that VAE correction.

[Raw budget probe](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/ca72d5212b33ab079f838144467a870de749e859/validation/rtx5090-20261017/evidence/host-budget-live-cgroup.json), [nested baseline](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/ca72d5212b33ab079f838144467a870de749e859/validation/rtx5090-20261017/evidence/sana-cgroup-baseline.json), [nested candidate](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/ca72d5212b33ab079f838144467a870de749e859/validation/rtx5090-20261017/evidence/sana-cgroup-patched.json), [scripts and raw outputs](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/ca72d5212b33ab079f838144467a870de749e859/validation/rtx5090-20261017/README.md).

Original isolated-unit entry points:

```bash
python test_host_budget_linux.py --baseline
python test_host_budget_linux.py
```

Those original runners select the respective main-source budget module with real Linux dependencies. The additional nightly unit run uses normal imports of the complete installed nightly package. The repeated SANA model run still uses SGLang 0.5.21 diffusion dependencies, the complete main-source budget module, and the same disclosed VAE prerequisite in both arms; it is not a full-nightly diffusion-model test. Upstream CI remains necessary.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speedup is claimed. Respecting the parent budget can intentionally select the existing pageable/staged transfer fallback. The goal is to honor headroom and the existing reserve, not to change inference math. GPU validation retained 400W and a 72°C stop threshold.

Targeted duplicate check: #37917 changes residency quotas, #36727 mapped offload/per-rank sharing, #37811 unified-pool residency, and #44540 HiCache physical ownership. Their inspected diffs do not change this function's binding-ancestor selection. [Pinned heads and search limits](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/ca72d5212b33ab079f838144467a870de749e859/validation/rtx5090-20261017/evidence/final-diff-audit.json).

- [x] Provide relevant accuracy/capacity and speed results below, with their measurement limits.

issues.title: [diffusion] vae: fix silently ignored --vae-tiling for Sana (AutoencoderDC)
issues.body:
### Motivation

Fixes #34482.

`--vae-tiling` was silently ignored for Sana models: the `AutoencoderDC` wrapper
does not proxy `enable_tiling` to the inner diffusers model, so the call raised
`AttributeError`, which (at the time this PR was opened) was swallowed by a bare
`except` in `DecodingStage`. On 8GB GPUs this turns a would-be-successful
generation into a fatal OOM after the full denoising loop has already run. See
the issue for the root-cause chain.

### Modifications

- `runtime/models/vaes/autoencoder_dc.py`: proxy `enable_tiling` /
  `disable_tiling` to the inner diffusers `AutoencoderDC`, which already
  implements them. `enable_tiling` is a no-op (with `warning_once`) when
  spatial-shard parallel decode is installed on this wrapper, since diffusers'
  `tiled_decode` running per-rank inside a height-sharded decoder breaks the
  halo exchange (mismatched collective rounds / wrong neighbours).
- `configs/models/vaes/sana.py`, `configs/pipeline_configs/sana.py`: update
  the two comments that claimed DC-AE tiling is unsupported.
- `test/unit/test_autoencoder_dc.py`: CPU-only unit test asserting the proxy
  forwards to the inner model and that the spatial-shard guard is a no-op.

### Scope / decisions

- **Default unchanged.** `SanaPipelineConfig.vae_tiling` stays `False`; tiling
  is opt-in via `--vae-tiling`. DC-AE is a 32x-compression autoencoder and
  tile seam quality / the benefit of diffusers' default 512 tile have not been
  validated, so a default flip does not belong in a bugfix.
- **`decoding.py` is no longer touched.** The v1 of this PR also replaced the
  bare `except` around `enable_tiling()` with a warning; main has since fixed
  that call site independently (specific `AttributeError` handling + warning),
  so that change is dropped here and the PR is now purely the wrapper-side fix.

### Test / Verification

- Before: `sglang generate --model-path Efficient-Large-Model/Sana_600M_512px_diffusers
  --prompt "..." --save-output --vae-tiling` — fatal OOM in `DecodingStage` on
  RTX 4070 Laptop 8GB (3/3 runs). Note: with DC-AE's 32x compression, tiling
  only engages at ≥1024x1024 (512x512 gives a 16x16 latent == `tile_latent_min`).
- After: same command (1024x1024) succeeds end-to-end; output image correct.
  This PR changes correctness (OOM → success), not performance; timings are
  not reported.
- `pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_autoencoder_dc.py` passes.
- pre-commit clean.

issues.title: [Feat] [AMD] diffusion: run Sol-Attn on ROCm gfx1201 with aiter's Sol kernel
issues.body:
> **Draft.** Stacked on #43687 (gfx1201 `AITER_SAGE`), which is stacked on #43686. Depends on the gfx1201 Sol-Attn op in aiter (parts 3-4 of the series: previews Shan2L/aiter#2 HIP kernel, Shan2L/aiter#3 code object), which follows ROCm/aiter#6390. This PR stays a draft until those are merged. Until then the diff includes the commits of the PRs below it; only the last commit belongs to this PR. Overall plan: [ROCm/aiter#6292](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6292#issuecomment-6106014448).

## Motivation

`SOL_ATTN` (NVlabs Sol-Attn, block-sparse attention with a dense guard for the first steps / layers) is rejected on ROCm, because its only kernel is the CUDA `sol_attn` package. aiter is adding `aiter.gfx1201_sol_attention` for Radeon RDNA4 (gfx1201: Radeon AI PRO R9700 / R9600D, Radeon RX 9070 series). It takes the same arguments as `sol_attn.sol_attn` with `thresh_type="diag"` (per-query-block routing on `tau`, plus sink tokens), and runs Sage-style INT8 QK^T / FP8 PV on the selected blocks.

Independent implementation: `aiter.gfx1201_sol_attention` is our own HIP and AMDGPU assembly implementation of the algorithm published in the Sol-Attn paper ([arXiv 2607.24027](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24027)). It contains no code from NVlabs/Sana or the `sol_attn` package; it only takes the same arguments. The CUDA path keeps using the `sol_attn` package as before.

## Modifications

- **Platform.** On ROCm, `SOL_ATTN` is selected when the GPU is gfx1201 and the installed aiter provides `gfx1201_sol_attention`. Otherwise it raises an explicit error, as before but with the requirement in the message.
- **Sparse path.** On ROCm, `SolAttnImpl` calls `aiter.gfx1201_sol_attention` with the configured `tau`, `sink_tokens`, `sink_start` and the layer's `softmax_scale`. Only `thresh_type="diag"` is supported (anything else raises); `kv_splits` is a CUDA scheduling knob and is not used.
- **Dense guard.** `dense_backend` gains an `aiter_sage` option, the default on ROCm. It reuses `AITERSageImpl` (so `gfx1201_sage_attention` with #43687), including the packed trailing-padding handling of `forward_varlen`.
- **Import.** `flash_attn_varlen_func` is imported lazily, so the module loads on ROCm.
- **Docs.** `attention_backends.mdx` lists gfx1201 support and the new `dense_backend` value.

CUDA behaviour is unchanged: the default dense backend stays `fa`, and the CUDA path still calls `sol_attn`.

Unit tests are in `test/unit/test_sol_attn_backend.py` and use stubbed `aiter` / platform, so they need no GPU. They cover platform selection and its errors, the arguments passed to `gfx1201_sol_attention`, the `thresh_type` check, and the `aiter_sage` dense guard for `forward` and `forward_varlen`.

## Accuracy and speed

MiniMax-H3, with the case parameters of `minimax_h3_t2va_2gpu_h100`: t2va, 1344x768, 4 s, 8 steps, seed 42, TP2, on 2x R9700 (PyTorch 2.11 / ROCm 7.15), same flags as that case. Sol rows: `--attention-backend sol_attn --attention-backend-config dense_steps=3 --component-attention-backends text_encoder=torch_sdpa,transformer=sol_attn` (default `tau=1.0`, dense layers `0,1`; `dense_steps` lowered from the default 10 because the case has 8 steps). Video PSNR and audio cosine are against the `torch_sdpa` run.

| attention | denoise stage | vs BF16 SDPA | video PSNR / audio cos vs SDPA run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `torch_sdpa` (BF16) | 152.3 s | 1.00x | - |
| `torch_sdpa`, K/V token order reversed (rounding-only noise floor) | 152.3 s | - | 34.41 dB / 0.991 |
| `aiter_sage` (#43687, aiter part 2) | 94.2 s | 1.62x | 32.14 dB / 0.897 |
| `sol_attn`, this PR, aiter part 3 (HIP kernel) | 91.2 s | 1.67x | 32.14 dB / 0.948 |
| `sol_attn`, this PR, aiter part 4 (code object) | 89.4 s | 1.70x | 32.30 dB / 0.946 |

At this short sequence (4 s video), 3 of 8 steps and 2 of 50 layers run dense, so Sol gains little over dense Sage. The sparse kernel pays off at longer sequences and more steps: on the 15 s / 362-frame ref2av case (29 steps) in LightX2V with its shipped MiniMax-H3 Sol config, the same kernels give 211.6 -> 63.7 s (part 3) / 60.8 s (part 4) per DiT step, against 89.1 s for dense Sage (part 2).

The R9700 runs used `sgl-kernel` built for gfx1201 (#43679), and the custom all-reduce was disabled because R9700s connect over PCIe (#43676).

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results (above).
- [ ] aiter parts 3 and 4 merged; then mark ready for review.

issues.title: [NVIDIA] perf: pipeline the extend-attention KV loads on Hopper
issues.body:
## Motivation

`num_stages` for the Triton extend-attention kernel has been hardcoded to `1` since the kernel was written, with no comment and no prior discussion that I could find. The KV loop body is a straight-line global-to-shared load of the K and V tiles followed by two dots, which is exactly the shape Triton can software pipeline. At one stage the global loads never overlap with compute, so the kernel waits on HBM. `decode_attention.py` right next door already carries tuned buckets with `num_stages=2`.

There is precedent for architecture-gated tuning in this same file: #26588 (Hopper block sizes for `Lq=129..256`), c1067f88 (gfx950 block sizes for `head_dim > 128`), #34741 (gfx950 tile shape on Triton 3.7).

## Modifications

One new helper next to `_get_block_sizes_for_extend_attention`, and one line changed at the call site in `extend_attention_fwd`. No signature changes, no kernel changes.

```python
def _num_stages_for_extend_attention(Lq: int) -> int:
    if not _is_cuda or CUDA_CAPABILITY[0] < 9:
        return 1
    return 3 if Lq <= 256 else 2
```

The condition order matters: `CUDA_CAPABILITY` is only defined inside the `if _is_cuda:` branch at the top of the module, so the short circuit is load-bearing.

HIP and pre-Hopper CUDA are untouched and keep `num_stages=1`. I have no ROCm hardware to measure on, and the gfx950 specialization is already fighting register spills per #34741, so raising the pipeline depth there is not something I want to guess at.

`extend_attention_fwd_unified` also has a hardcoded `num_stages = 1`. I left it alone deliberately, since I did not benchmark that path.

## Accuracy Tests

`num_stages` is a scheduling hint and must not change results, so I checked with exact comparison rather than a tolerance. For every configuration I took an output fingerprint (sum, max absolute value, and the sum over a strided slice) at `num_stages` 1, 2, and 3 and compared them for equality.

**All 16 configurations produced identical fingerprints. Zero mismatches.**

I was not able to run `test/registered/attention/` locally: those tests pull a tokenizer from HuggingFace and the machine I benchmark on has no outbound internet access. CI should cover that once this is labeled.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

NVIDIA H200 (sm_90), `shared_memory_per_block_optin = 232448`, bf16, `n = 16384`, fresh prompt with no prefix, 4 warmup and 12 timed iterations. Times in milliseconds.

| head_dim | q/kv heads | BLOCK_M | BLOCK_N | ns=1 | ns=2 | ns=3 | best |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 16/8 | 128 | 64 | 4.231 | 3.982 | **3.587** | 1.18x |
| 64 | 32/4 | 128 | 64 | 7.960 | 7.499 | **6.771** | 1.18x |
| 128 | 16/8 | 128 | 64 | 5.809 | 5.750 | **5.199** | 1.12x |
| 128 | 32/4 | 128 | 64 | 10.895 | 10.686 | **10.045** | 1.08x |
| 256 | 16/8 | 64 | 64 | 18.227 | 16.228 | **14.500** | 1.26x |
| 256 | 32/4 | 64 | 64 | 35.077 | 31.708 | **28.354** | 1.24x |
| 512 | 16/8 | 32 | 64 | 45.960 | **31.760** | OOM | 1.45x |
| 512 | 32/4 | 32 | 64 | 91.029 | **61.047** | OOM | 1.49x |

The OOM at `Lq=512, num_stages=3` is `Required: 299008, Hardware limit: 232448`. That is the reason the helper caps at 2 above `Lq=256` rather than going to 3 everywhere.

### A note on the sliding-window path

I also measured all eight shapes above with `sliding_window_size=1024`. There the gain is 1.00x to 1.03x, essentially nothing. That is expected rather than disappointing: on current `main` the stage-2 loop still walks from block 0 and relies on `SKIP_TILE` to skip the body, so most iterations load nothing at all and there is nothing to pipeline.

Once the loop is bounded by the window (#34462), that path becomes load-bound again and `num_stages` starts paying there too. With that bound applied I measured a further 1.17x from `num_stages=2` at `head_dim=256`, `window=1024`, `n=27000`. The two changes compose; this one stands on its own for the non-windowed case.

## What this does not cover

- One GPU model (H200), one sequence length, two head configurations.
- The `Lq <= 256` threshold is the boundary I measured, not something derived from a shared-memory formula. Other Hopper parts share the same limit so it should hold, but I only have one kind of card to say that with.
- No ROCm validation, hence the architecture gate.

issues.title: [diffusion] vae: retry decode with tiling once on OOM instead of failing
issues.body:
## Motivation

Today, when a full-frame VAE decode hits CUDA OOM, `DecodingStage` logs
advice (added in #35353) and the whole generation dies — after all the
denoising compute has already been spent. On consumer GPUs this is the
most common terminal failure mode: on an 8GB RTX 4070 Laptop, Sana 600M
at its default 1024×1024 reliably survives 20 denoising steps and then
crashes in exactly this spot (#34482). The advice can only help on the
*next* run; the current request is unrecoverable.

This PR turns that advice into a one-shot automatic fallback: if tiling
is off and the VAE supports toggling it at runtime, free the cache,
enable tiling, and retry the decode once. The worst case is the same
crash as today; the best case is a completed request with tiled output.

**Open design question for maintainers**: tiled decode can introduce
minor seams at tile boundaries, so this trades a guaranteed crash for a
possible (small, bounded) quality difference, and does so automatically.
The retry logs a prominent warning telling the user what happened and
how to make the choice explicit (`--vae-tiling`, or freeing components
via offload flags). If you'd rather gate the auto-retry behind a flag or
env var, happy to adjust — took "crash is strictly worse" as the default
stance. cc @mickqian who authored the advice-based handling in #35353.

## Modifications

`runtime/pipelines_core/stages/decoding.py` (one hunk inside
`DecodingStage.decode`):

- In the existing OOM `except` branch: if `--vae-tiling` is off and the
  VAE exposes **both** `enable_tiling` and `disable_tiling`, mark the
  decode for a single tiled retry instead of re-raising.
- The retry runs after the `except` block exits (not inside it), so the
  original exception's traceback — which pins the failed attempt's
  activation tensors — is released before `empty_cache()` and the second
  attempt.
- The retry empties the device cache, enables tiling, decodes, and
  restores the untiled state in a `finally` — so a VAE shared across
  requests is never left silently tiled.
- The retry calls `self.vae.decode(latents)` directly instead of going
  through `_get_vae_decode_fn`: that helper only (optionally) wraps
  `vae.decode` in torch.compile, and a graph compiled for the untiled
  path is unsound once `enable_tiling()` changes control flow —
  recompiling while already under memory pressure is its own risk.
- Behavior is unchanged in every other case: tiling already on → same
  advice + raise as today; VAE can't toggle tiling at runtime → same
  advice + raise; non-OOM exceptions propagate untouched.
- Why `hasattr` for the capability probe rather than the
  `try/except AttributeError` style used earlier in this function: the
  retry decision must be made *before* choosing to swallow the OOM, and
  it must confirm `disable_tiling` exists too, or the finally-restore
  above would be impossible and the VAE would stay tiled for subsequent
  requests. VAE wrappers are genuinely heterogeneous here (see #34482 /
  #34514 — AutoencoderDC only recently grew these methods).

`test/unit/test_decode_oom_fallback.py` (new): 6 unit tests with a mock
VAE covering: OOM→success retry (exact call order `decode` →
`enable_tiling` → `decode` → `disable_tiling`, plus the user-facing
warning), retry-also-OOMs (state still restored, error propagates),
no-retry when tiling already on, no-retry when `enable_tiling` missing,
no-retry when only `disable_tiling` missing, and non-OOM exceptions
propagating immediately. Picked up automatically by the `unit` suite
(directory discovery, no registry edit needed).

## Accuracy Tests

No change on the normal path — the fallback only activates where today's
behavior is a crash. The tiled output produced by the fallback is
identical to what a user gets today by passing `--vae-tiling` explicitly.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No happy-path impact: one extra local bool; the fallback work happens
only after an OOM that is terminal today.

Unit tests (container `lmsysorg/sglang:dev`, repo mounted, on top of
`881cbfe54c`):

```
python -m pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_decode_oom_fallback.py -v
# 6 passed

python -m pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_decoding_stage_parallelism.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_vae_fast_path_gate.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_vae_spatial_parallel_decode.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_vae_decoder_store.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_vae_loader_decode_dtype.py -q
# 38 passed, 12 subtests passed
```

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

issues.title: [Bugfix] Thread LTX-2 linear prefixes for ModelOpt NVFP4
issues.body:
## Motivation

Current SGLang main contains the ModelOpt NVFP4 scale-layout conversion for
non-packed-QKV DiTs, but LTX-2 does not propagate checkpoint-compatible layer
prefixes into its quantizable parallel-linear modules.

This breaks two coupled contracts:

1. `ModelOptQuantConfig.is_layer_excluded()` cannot match checkpoint exclusion
   patterns such as `transformer_blocks.0.*`.
2. `uses_flux1_scale_layout` cannot recognize the affected LTX-2 layers because
   it requires a prefix beginning with `transformer_blocks.` or
   `single_transformer_blocks.`.

The resulting load-time packed-versus-dense shape assertion can look like a
checkpoint architecture mismatch, but the serialized `(2048, 1024)` FP4
weight is the packed representation of a logical `(2048, 2048)` matrix.

Sibling DiTs including Flux, Flux2, GLM-Image, Qwen-Image, and the SANA-WM
refiner already construct their blocks with `transformer_blocks.<index>`.

## Modifications

- Construct each LTX-2 block with `transformer_blocks.<index>`.
- Propagate prefixes through attention `to_q`, `to_k`, `to_v`,
  `to_gate_logits`, and `to_out.0`.
