issues.title: [Feat] lfm3: Add text, vision, audio and Omni support
issues.body:
## Summary

Add native text generation for the LFM3 family in SGLang.

| Model | Inputs | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LFM3 | Text | Text |
| LFM3-VL | Text, images, video | Text |
| LFM3-Audio | Text, audio | Text |
| LFM3-Omni | Text, images, audio, video, including video soundtracks | Text |

Uses stock Transformers with `--trust-remote-code` to load the checkpoint-provided configs and processors.

## Implementation

- Shared LFM3 backbone with gated short convolutions, full/sliding-window attention, and SGLang's hybrid cache integration. Includes CuTe DSL convolution kernels and a PyTorch fallback.
- Vision and audio encoders, projectors, and checkpoint loading. Omni reuses these components and the text backbone.
- Multimodal preprocessing uses the checkpoint's Transformers processors and chat template. Omni supports mixed inputs and video/audio interleaving.
- FlashInfer defaults to paged prefill for correct sliding-window attention.

## Usage

Choose a checkpoint for the input modalities you need:

| Model | Checkpoint |
| --- | --- |
| Text | [LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B) |
| Vision | [LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B) |
| Audio | [LiquidAI/LFM3-Audio-2B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-Audio-2B) |
| Omni | [LiquidAI/LFM3-Omni-2B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-Omni-2B) |

For example, launch Omni:

```bash
sglang serve \
  --model-path LiquidAI/LFM3-Omni-2B \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto \
  --served-model-name lfm3 \
  --port 30000
```

Send requests through `/v1/chat/completions`. This client works with each model; select supported content below. Replace example media URLs with files reachable by the server.

```python
import base64
from pathlib import Path
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:30000/v1", api_key="EMPTY")

def ask(content, **kwargs):
    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="lfm3",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": content}],
        temperature=0,
        max_tokens=256,
        **kwargs,
    )
    print(response.choices[0].message.content)

# Text
ask("What is the capital of Poland?")

# Image
image = {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "https://your-host/image.jpg"}}
ask([image, {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image."}])

# Video
video = {"type": "video_url", "video_url": {"url": "https://your-host/video.mp4"}}
ask([video, {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this video."}])

# Audio
encoded = base64.b64encode(Path("question.wav").read_bytes()).decode("ascii")
audio = {"type": "input_audio", "input_audio": {"data": encoded, "format": "wav"}}
ask([audio, {"type": "text", "text": "Answer the spoken question in text."}])

# Omni: image + spoken question
ask([image, audio])

# Omni: video with its soundtrack
ask(
    [video, {"type": "text", "text": "Summarize what happens and what is said."}],
    extra_body={"use_audio_in_video": True},
)
```

For transcription, launch LFM3-Audio and call the existing endpoint:

```bash
curl http://localhost:30000/v1/audio/transcriptions \
  -F model=lfm3 -F file=@question.wav
```

## Validation

Validation below was run on development checkpoints. FP16, TP1, H100, FlashInfer against Transformers; serving uses stock Transformers 5.19.0 with `--trust-remote-code`.

| Suite | Prefill/decode checks | ROUGE-L |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text | 4/4 | 4/4 |
| Vision | 16/16 | 14/16 |
| Audio → text | 5/5 | 5/5 |
| Omni → text | 22/22 | 20/22 |

All 211 targeted CPU tests and 259 subtests passed. Live tool calling with both parsers set to `auto` and startup rejection probes passed. Vision ROUGE compares raw output with parsing disabled.

Triton also passed all 20 text/vision prefill and decode checks in FP16 on H100 with 1,024-token prefill chunks, including a long prompt beyond the 256-token sliding window. All generated outputs matched the FlashInfer run; the same two vision ROUGE failures remained. Audio and Omni were not tested with Triton.

Additional coverage: BF16 Omni smoke tests on H100; independent BF16 text/VL validation on H200, including TP2 text.

issues.title: [Fix] qwen4_exp: Split the PLE prefill short conv under the int32 limit
issues.body:
## Motivation

Serving Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on ROCm, a prefill batch that holds many short requests next to one long request kills the scheduler on both TP ranks:

```text
RuntimeError: Expected canUse32BitIndexMath(input) && canUse32BitIndexMath(output)
  File ".../sglang/srt/models/qwen4_exp.py", in _short_conv
    conv_output = F.conv1d(
```

The PLE short conv pads every request in the batch to the longest one:

- conv input: `[num_requests, 10240, longest_extend + 9]` (10240 = `hidden_size × hc_count`, 9 = conv state length)
- PyTorch does not send dilated grouped convs to MIOpen, so on ROCm `F.conv1d` runs the native depthwise kernel, which requires fewer than 2**31 − 1 elements in its input and output.
- The limit is passed once `num_requests × (longest_extend + 9) ≥ 209,716`. A batch of fresh 8k prompts never gets there (the default 16,384-token chunk holds at most 3 of them). Prefix-cache hits do: 94 requests of which one extends 2,223 tokens are enough, and so are 42 requests of which one extends 4,985 tokens.
- `bench_serving --warmup-requests 128` produces such batches: it sends 128 copies of one prompt, which then hit the radix cache.

Observed: `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4`, TP2, MI355X, random 8k-in/1k-out at concurrency 128 crashes in the bench warmup on the unmodified image with the commands below. The crashing batch logs no "Prefill batch" line, because prefill stats are logged after the forward.

Scope:

- Models: `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next checkpoints). The MTP draft has no PLE layers.
- Code path: ordinary prefill/extend and target-verify batches of the PLE short conv. Decode is unchanged.
- Platforms: ROCm. On NVIDIA, PyTorch sends the over-limit depthwise conv to cuDNN when cuDNN ≥ 9.3 with the v8 API, so only older cuDNN setups reach the same check.
- Prior art: #43032 (open) replaces the padded path with a packed varlen Triton kernel. Its motivation is memory, and it is enabled only when `is_cuda()`, so ROCm keeps the padded `F.conv1d` path. No issue or PR covers this crash.

## Modifications

- `qwen4_exp.py`: new `_short_conv1d()` runs the depthwise conv in pieces whose input stays under the limit.
  - Rows are independent, so it splits by rows first.
  - If one row alone is too long (chunked prefill off, prompt ≥ 209,707 tokens), it also splits that row's output columns, each piece carrying the 9-column conv halo.
  - Batches under the limit take the same single `F.conv1d` call as before.
- The padded memory (`num_requests × longest_extend × 10240` per temporary) is unchanged; #43032 addresses it on NVIDIA.
- New CPU test `test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen4_exp_short_conv_split.py`.
  - Runs the real `_prepare_ple_batch` and `Qwen4ExpPLELayer._short_conv` on a 4-request batch with lengths `[37, 1, 3, 2]`.
  - Lowers the limit to 200 (row split) and 100 (row and column split).
  - Checks that every `F.conv1d` input is under the limit and that the output equals the single-call result.
  - On main it fails: one call, `AssertionError: 1 not greater than 1`.

## Accuracy Tests

- The split is exact: each output element is computed from the same 4 inputs and weights by the same kernel.
- CPU test: the output is `torch.equal` to the single call (integer-valued data, so no rounding differences).
- MI355X, one GPU, the conv at the limit (bf16, 10240 channels, kernel 4, dilation 3):
  - unsplit `F.conv1d`, 94 rows × width 2231 (2,147,471,360 elements): runs;
  - 94 rows × width 2232 (2,148,433,920 elements): raises `canUse32BitIndexMath`;
  - `_short_conv1d` at 94 × 2232: 16.1 ms, output `torch.equal` to two unsplit half-batch calls.
- No task-level accuracy eval was run: the change is exact, and batches under the limit take the unchanged single call.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Setup:
- Image: `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x-20261021`, PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm7.2; its `qwen4_exp.py` is byte-identical to SGLang `a2e4ffbcea`, and the changed code is identical on main.
- Hardware: 2× MI355X (gfx950).
- Model: `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4`, revision `b2091c3809eb51902f46a163973362d8176f9e58`.
- Baseline: the image as shipped. Patched: this change applied to `qwen4_exp.py` (the GPU runs used a revision with two extra `max(1, …)` clamps on the piece sizes, which never take effect).
- One server launch per row below, same request stream (2,832,445 input, 353,963 output tokens).

| Server | Completed | Output tok/s | TTFT mean / median (ms) | TPOT mean (ms) | Largest prefill batch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | crashed in warmup (both ranks) | — | — | — | — |
| This change | 384 / 384 | 2325.7 | 4731 / 645 | 48.3 | 125 requests |
| Baseline + `--prefill-max-requests 12` | 384 / 384 | 2323.3 | 4603 / 664 | 48.5 | 12 requests |

- The patched run's 125-request batch (10,391 new and 920,576 cached tokens) sits at the point where the baseline crashed; no out-of-memory error at `--mem-fraction-static 0.9`.
- This change completes the row at the same output throughput as the flag workaround (2325.7 vs 2323.3 tok/s, one run each).
- `--prefill-max-requests 12` avoids the crash only while the chunk stays 16,384 tokens (12 × (16,384 + 9) = 196,716 < 209,716); this change covers any batch shape.
- Batches under the limit run the same single `F.conv1d` call as before.

Commands:

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 \
  --revision b2091c3809eb51902f46a163973362d8176f9e58 --tp 2 --quantization quark \
  --trust-remote-code --context-length 131072 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --enable-multimodal --limit-mm-data-per-request '{"image": 1}' \
  --mm-process-config '{"image": {"min_pixels": 65536, "max_pixels": 16777216}}' \
  --mm-enable-dp-encoder --port 8003

python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 8003 \
  --model amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0.8 --seed 6 \
  --max-concurrency 128 --num-prompts 384 --warmup-requests 128 --request-rate inf
```

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations): not needed (no new flag or API).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

issues.title: [Feat] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: Avoid padded PLE prefill activations
issues.body: ## Summary This PR fixes Qwen3.8/Qwen4Exp PLE prefill temporary activation amplification for mixed-length batches. The current PLE short-conv prefill path materializes packed tokens as a dense tensor: ```text [num_requests, max_query_length, ple_channels] ``` This means short requests are padded to the longest request in the batch. For skewed mixed-length batches, the temporary activation memory scales with: ```text num_requests × max_query_length × ple_channels ``` instead of: ```text sum(query_lengths) × ple_channels ``` This can allocate several GiB of temporary tensors and cause OOM even when KV cache utilization is still low. This PR adds a packed varlen Triton path for ordinary PLE prefill so short-conv memory and compute scale with the actual scheduled tokens. ### Nsight Systems serving trace To verify that the packed kernel is selected in the serving path, we profiled a single HTTP batched request containing four sequences: ```text query lengths = [8192, 1, 1, 1], new sequences = 4, new tokens = 8195, cached tokens = 0 ``` The following traces compare the same TP rank and GPU. The baseline uses the existing padded PyTorch path: The packed-varlen implementation replaces the large padded concatenation and cuDNN depthwise convolution with the varlen convolution and state writeback kernels: The target PLE short-conv kernel chain changed as follows: | Path | Kernel | GPU time | |---|---|---:| | Padded baseline | `CatArrayBatchedCopy` | 4.427 ms | | Padded baseline | `conv_depthwise2d_forward_kernel_generic` | 5.881 ms | | Packed varlen | `_qwen4_varlen_conv_kernel` | 0.714 ms | | Packed varlen | `_qwen4_varlen_state_writeback_kernel` | 0.020 ms | | **Baseline total** | | **10.308 ms** | | **Packed-varlen total** | | **0.735 ms** | For this serving trace, the target PLE short-conv GPU time decreased by approximately **92.9%**, corresponding to a **14.0x** speedup for this kernel chain. The asynchronous PLE embedding gather and surrounding model computation remain unchanged. These measurements demonstrate replacement of the target padded short-conv path; they do not represent a 14x end-to-end model speedup. ## Changes - Add a packed varlen PLE prefill short-conv Triton kernel. - Add a separate state-writeback kernel for main and radix-tracking short-conv states. - Preserve the existing decode and MTP target-verify paths. - Preserve the existing PyTorch path as a fallback. - Add live `query_start_loc` metadata for breakable prefill CUDA Graph replay. - Enable the fused path only for supported NVIDIA CUDA BF16 inputs. - Add direct correctness tests for mixed-length, equal-length, empty rows, chunked prefill, radix tracking, FP32 state storage, fallback, and graph live metadata. The change is limited to five files and does not modify the scheduler, cache ownership, MTP state-commit protocol, N-gram logic, or PLE gate logic. ## Correctness The packed implementation was compared against the existing padded PyTorch path using real Qwen3.8 PLE dimensions: ```text channels = 10240 kernel size = 4 dilation = 3 state length = 9 dtype = BF16 GPU = NVIDIA H20 ``` Covered cases include: - mixed-length batches - equal-length batches - chunked prefill - empty request rows - radix state tracking - FP32 state storage with BF16 materialization semantics All tested cases produced element-wise identical outputs and final states: ```text output max absolute error = 0 state max absolute error = 0 torch.equal(output) = True torch.equal(state) = True ``` Service-level validation also covered ordinary mixed-length prefill, NEXTN MTP3, decode CUDA Graph, breakable prefill CUDA Graph, and target-verify CUDA Graph. Baseline and feature outputs had identical hashes, and NEXTN MTP3 preserved `accept length = 4.0` and `accept rate = 1.0`. ## PLE short-conv performance The packed varlen path reduces PLE prefill short-conv latency by removing dense padding, transpose/concatenation, packed-output gathering, and separate PyTorch state updates. The following H20 BF16 results compare the existing padded prefill short-conv path with the packed varlen convolution and state-writeback kernels. Both sides exclude the common SiLU operation. | Query lengths | Padded path | Packed varlen | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:| | `[8192, 1, 1, 1]` | 11.84 ms | 0.70 ms | 16.85x | | `[4096, 2048, 1024, 512]` | 6.57 ms | 0.66 ms | 9.94x | | `[2048, 2048, 2048, 2048]` | 4.11 ms | 0.70 ms | 5.86x | | Chunked prefill, `8192` as `4 × 2048` | 4.34 ms | 0.84 ms | 5.14x | | Radix state tracking, `[4096, 2048, 1024, 512]` | 6.59 ms | 0.67 ms | 9.81x | ## Memory results For the most skewed kernel workload: ```text query lengths = [8192, 1, 1, 1] ``` | Metric | Padded path | Packed varlen | |---|---:|---:| | Incremental peak allocated memory | 2081.5 MiB | 160.1 MiB | | Mean short-conv latency | 11.84 ms | 0.70 ms | In the mixed-length serving matrix, process-level GPU peak memory changed from: ```text 97,039 MiB -> 90,097 MiB ``` This reduced the observed peak by approximately 6.8 GiB. The padded implementation also OOMed at `--mem-fraction-static 0.85` in the tested mixed-length workload because of a roughly 3 GiB short-conv temporary allocation. The packed implementation completed successfully. ## End-to-end check For a mixed-length workload: ```text [L, L/8, L/32, L/256, L/1024, 8] ``` with TP8 + EP8, `--chunked-prefill-size 32768`, and 64 output tokens: | Maximum input length | Input throughput change | Median E2E change | |---:|---:|---:| | 32K | +7.32% | -6.91% | This PR is primarily a memory/OOM fix, not a general long-context throughput optimization. ## Usage No new command-line option is required. The packed varlen path is selected automatically for supported Qwen3.8/Qwen4Exp PLE ordinary prefill batches on NVIDIA CUDA with BF16 inputs. issues.title: [short-conv] Radix mamba-cache track for multi-entry conv state (1/3)
issues.body:
> **Stack:** this PR (1/3) → #36952 (2/3, cuda-graph) → #36953 (3/3, ZAYA1).
> A fork cannot set an upstream branch as a PR base, so #36952 and #36953 also
> contain this commit; merge in order.

## Motivation

`ShortConvAttnBackend` serves models whose per-request state is one or more causal short convs with no SSM component — LFM2's depthwise gated conv, and ZAYA1's two-stage grouped conv plus its one-token value lag. Only the single-conv, single-window case was wired for the mamba radix cache's `extra_buffer` strategy, so a short-conv model could not checkpoint state at a chunk-aligned length and had to run on `no_buffer`.

This is **1 of 3** in a series adding ZAYA1 support. It is the shared short-conv infrastructure; it stands alone and contains no ZAYA1 model code.

## Modifications

**Multi-entry track snapshot.** The extend-side snapshot becomes one index tensor per conv entry, each gathering its own window from its own input tensor, with every entry's window ending at the same chunk-aligned track position. The decode-side snapshot flattens the pool's `[n_layers, n_slots, ...]` view to `[n_layers * n_slots, ...]` and copies every layer in one launch, since a model with dozens of conv layers is launch-bound at decode.

**`MambaAttnBackendBase.has_temporal_state`.** A pure short conv allocates a zero-element `temporal` tensor, so the SSM track-index build — five device-to-host copies per extend step — has nothing to do. Every SSM backend leaves this `True` and is unaffected.

**A persistent extend cu-seqlens buffer**, alongside the existing decode and verify ones, so a kernel reading them from inside a captured graph does not bake the address of a per-step temporary. Its tail is flooded with the final offset so a request slot past the current batch reads `start == end`.

**`mamba_cache_chunk_size` stops taking the model's scan length as the radix caching granularity.** A conv-only model reports `mamba_chunk_size == 1`, which is honest — there is no chunked recurrence — but useless as a caching point, and below the conv window besides, so the backend refuses to start. Those models take the generic FLA chunk raised to clear the widest conv window. Every model with a real scan (`mamba_chunk_size > 1`) and every model that declares none keeps `max(scan_chunk, page_size)` exactly.

**Two refusals moved to resolution.** The track cannot serve a captured prefill graph (its gather's row count is `mamba_track_mask.sum()`, which would freeze at whatever capture saw) or speculative decoding (no per-draft-token accept hook). Both are pure config combinations, so they are asserted in `ServerArgs._validate_mamba_extra_buffer` alongside the existing arch/device/track-interval checks rather than raised from a backend constructor — an operator hears about them before the weights load. Gated on the short-conv archs, since an SSM arch verifies through `prepare_mamba_track_for_verify`.

**Graph-stable buffers are sized before capture, not in `init_cuda_graph_state`.** That hook has callers only in the decode runner and the speculative draft runners, but `cuda_graph_setup` captures prefill **first** — so the extend cu-seqlens, the int64 slot view and the prefix mask were all still `None` at prefill capture and the fallback `torch.empty` branch fired, baking storage that is freed the moment capture ends. Any backend whose captured prefill kernels read them is exposed. `InklingShortConvAttnBackend` already carried this fix locally, with the comment *"the base only sizes this from init_cuda_graph_state, which the prefill graph never calls"* — this is the base-class version of a workaround one backend had already been forced into. Sizing takes the max of the prefill request bound and the decode runner's largest capture bs, because growing a buffer after a graph captured it moves the address that graph reads.

LFM2 calls the two hooks. It stays off `extra_buffer` until validated on hardware, so they are inert for it today.

**The extend host mirrors are staged, not resolved.** `init_forward_metadata` ran `.tolist()` on the slot indices every extend step -- a device-to-host sync on the step's critical path -- to build host mirrors that only the reference extend host loop reads; a fused prefill conv never touches them. The backend now stages the (already-host) prefix list and resolves the sync lazily in `extend_host_mirrors()`, memoized per step. The default path no longer pays the sync; a fallback pays it once, on first use.

## Accuracy Test

Verified on H200 (torch 2.13.0+cu130 / triton 3.7.1):

```
test_short_conv_track.py (new)              16 passed
test_server_args.py                        185 passed
test_supplied_instance_exposure_ratchet.py   2 passed
test_global_config_read_ratchet.py           2 passed
test_model_overrides.py                     88 passed
```

The new test file pins the index arithmetic — where the extend snapshot reads from, what lands in the track slot, and the all-layers decode row copy — against a torch reference, with no model and no live `ModelRunner`.

The buffer fix is additionally validated end to end: without it, ZAYA1-74B with a captured prefill graph and the fused extend conv is a **CUDA illegal memory access that kills the server**; with it, the server boots and single-request prefill bit-matches the eager reference.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

No throughput claim. This PR enables a capability (`extra_buffer` for short-conv models) rather than changing an existing path; the hot-path changes are the removal of five device-to-host copies per extend step for backends with no SSM state, and one fewer device-to-host sync per extend step for models that stay on a fused prefill conv.

issues.body:
## Motivation

SANA-Video eager inference inherits the image model's restriction that enables LN+modulation fusion only on CUDA-graph streams. For the tested video activation, `[1, 32760, 2240]`, the existing fused kernel passes live exactness verification. It preserves the required contiguous input copy while fusing LayerNorm, scale and shift, avoiding the intermediate tensors between those operations. A separate final-head profile replaces 82 ATen LayerNorm chains with 82 existing fused kernels per CFG iteration, reducing the total GPU kernel count from 2,309 to 2,063.

The image restriction remains the default: prior image measurements in #34015 found an eager regression. Video opts in at its two transformer-block normalization sites and its final modulated normalization. Main's existing video BCG path already uses this fusion; this PR extends eager execution rather than claiming new BCG support.

Frozen SGLang main: `af21e2b989e482cfdce39689126562f2209d53ac`.
Final tested head: `e0d694593a65cb5b463c4011b84ee50abefa5e43`.
Frozen vLLM-Omni: `817d4c17feb702289a2d2b2cbacfd594c262b7a7`.

## Modifications

- Add an optional `allow_eager=False` keyword to the existing `sana_ln_modulate` wrapper and reuse its existing stream/device/compile dispatch helper.
- Opt in only from SANA-Video's three call sites. Preserve the fused kernel, per-signature live-ATen exactness gate, unverified-capture protection and mismatch fallback.
- Extend the existing four-shape wrapper test across both stream policies, with fresh gate state, default image inference and grad-enabled fallback checks. Reuse the generic gate tests and update the existing kernel README.

No new kernel, environment variable, tuning setting or unrelated refactor is included.

## Accuracy Tests

One physical RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPU0, SM120, 97,887 MiB, 600 W, driver 595.84. GPU1 remains idle. SGLang uses PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 / Triton 3.8.0; Omni uses PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. Dependencies and resolved launch commands are archived.

The common checkpoint is `Efficient-Large-Model/SANA-Video_2B_480p_diffusers@db5f398b13ca086d09a50ce156c20527773841b1`, with verified file hashes. Both native pipelines run 832×480, 81 frames at 16 fps, 50 steps, CFG 6, CPU seed 1101, empty negative prompt, maximum 300 selected text tokens, batch/concurrency 1. DiT and text encoder are BF16; VAE, initial noise and solver arithmetic retain the native FP32 contract. The effective positive text includes the same motion-score instruction. Both encode H.264/yuv420p with CRF 0; native encoder versions differ and all quality comparisons use the same decoder.

Actual runtime observations establish equal token IDs/masks, initial noise, timesteps and sigmas. Native BF16 text-encoder outputs and subsequent model predictions differ across frameworks; they were measured, not replaced. The observer preserves all eight qualification MP4s byte-for-byte.

Cross-framework admission requires **every frame** to satisfy SSIM ≥0.92 and PSNR ≥24 dB:

| Prompt | Mean / minimum SSIM | Mean / minimum PSNR (dB) | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| short | 0.956517 / 0.930914 | 30.7329 / 28.4207 | pass |
| long | 0.962520 / 0.951014 | 30.9685 / 29.1087 | pass |
| Chinese | 0.939182 / 0.920909 | 26.7774 / 23.5768 | **fail at frames 26–28; excluded from performance admission** |

This does not claim that different quality settings match one another or that the baseline's semantic generation defects are fixed.

Omni uses its native synchronized method wrappers, with one steady diagnostic request per English prompt. Native stage boundaries differ across frameworks; no diagnostic timing replaces primary E2E.
